silhouette.reason: panel-1: Reads instantly as an RTS faction HQ from the strategy camera: gabled hall flanked by two conical-roof towers with finials, portico, banners, a tank in a bay, an infantry squad and a crystal resource node. The front elevation silhouette (towers + gable) is distinctive. Side view loses it: the hall and towers merge into one block and the yard props vanish into a flat line. | panel-2: From the RTS camera the set reads at once: a gabled hall with two cone-roofed round towers, porch, banners, a tank, an infantry squad and a crystal resource node, each with a distinct outline. The front elevation is strong. The side elevation is a plain box with a flat roof line, the infantry are near-identical upright pegs, and the perimeter wall is a uniform low bar that adds no shape. | panel-3: From the RTS camera (3/4 front, far LOD2) it reads instantly as a faction HQ: twin conical-roofed towers, gabled red hall with a porch, banners, a tank, troops and a resource crystal node. Front view is a clean symmetric castle-hall read. The side and plan silhouettes are flat (a long low box plus a slab), and the hall itself is a generic barn shape; the towers are small for a stronghold so the outline lacks a dominant hero feature.
fixes: Raise the towers or add crenellation/dormers so they separate from the hall in side view
Give the yard a tall readable element (watchtower, radio mast, gate arch) to break the flat plinth outline
Make the crystal cluster larger so the resource reads from the top camera
Break the hall's side roof line with a chimney, dormer or ridge vent
Vary the infantry poses and give at least one a distinct outline (kneeling, officer with flag)
Add wall piers or a gate post taller than the wall run so the perimeter has rhythm
Give the tank a longer gun barrel so it reads from the side at distance
Raise the towers ~25% above the ridge and add crenellation or a machicolation band so the outline names a fortified HQ
Add a central tall element (bell tower, radio mast or keep) to break the long ridge line
Give the perimeter wall a gatehouse or corner posts so the plan outline is not a bare slab

proportions.reason: panel-1: Scale relationships mostly hold: soldiers ~1.8 m against a ~6 m tank and a ~2.5 m door. But the infantry are peg-doll figures with oversized helmet-heads and stubby limbs, the hall windows are large and identical for a stone fortress, the towers have only tiny slit openings with no ground entrance on one, and the courtyard is a large empty slab relative to the building footprint. | panel-2: Building, tank and soldiers sit in a believable RTS scale relationship and the hall's storey height, door and porch work against the figures. The soldiers are mannequins: ball heads, tube limbs, block torsos, with stiff identical stances, which is the weakest proportion in the scene. The ground-floor windows are large and sit low for the wall height, the towers are thick for their height and have one tiny door, the tank turret is big for its hull with a stubby gun, and the crystals are as tall as the soldiers' whole bodies with no mass logic in the rock. | panel-3: Building storey heights, window and door sizes read plausibly against the 5 m grid; walls, sandbags and crates are at believable scale. The tank is small (roughly WWII light/medium size) but fine for RTS. Infantry are stylised with oversized heads and stiff stick limbs and look slightly short beside the door. The towers are narrow and stubby relative to the hall.
fixes: Rework infantry with correct 7.5-head proportions, defined shoulders, hands and faces
Vary window sizes by storey and add a tower door/stair at ground level
Fill the yard to the footprint: vehicle pad markings, crates, fuel drums, a sentry post
Rebuild the infantry with a shaped head and helmet, tapered limbs, shoulders and a pelvis; vary stance
Shrink the hall windows about 15% and raise the sill line
Slim the towers or raise them one more course above the eave
Lengthen the tank gun to roughly hull length and reduce turret width
Seat the crystals in a larger rock base with a spread of sizes
Rebalance infantry to ~7 heads tall with defined shoulders and bent-knee stances
Widen tower diameter ~15% and lengthen the cone roofs
Check the porch door height against a 1.8 m figure; it reads close to 3 m

materials.reason: panel-1: Clay roof tiles, ashlar stone, timber framing, concrete barriers, painted tank and glowing amber crystals separate well by hue and value; the emissive windows sell interior light. But everything shares one matte response: the tank shows no metallic edge sheen, crystals look like opaque plastic rather than translucent, the gold finials and sun disc are flat yellow, and the ground slab is untextured grey. | panel-2: Clay roof tiles, ashlar stone, dark timber, cloth banners, painted tank steel and glowing crystal all separate by hue and value, and the faction red ties the set together. Lit windows are flat orange rectangles with no glass or interior depth, the stone is one hue across hall, towers, wall and ground slab so the pad looks like the same material as the walls, the tank reads as matte plastic with little metal response, and the crystals are flat-shaded orange without translucency or internal glow gradient. | panel-3: Stone blocks, timber framing, red tile roof, glowing windows, painted tank armour with rust, sandbag cloth and amber crystals all separate by hue and value, coherent in a stylised RTS palette. Glass is emissive-only with no reflection; the tank metal has little specular; the crystals are flat orange with no translucency or glow, which undersells the resource node.
fixes: Give the tank hull metallic edge wear and lower roughness on scuffs
Make crystals translucent with a brighter core and specular facets
Add a cobble or packed-earth texture with tyre ruts to the ground; make finials metallic gold
Give windows a recessed pane with a gradient glow and a mullion with depth
Shift the ground slab to a different hue and roughness from the wall stone (packed earth or darker paving)
Raise metalness and add edge highlights on the tank, with darker rubber or steel tracks
Add emissive falloff and a lighter core to the crystals
Add a second timber tone for the porch posts
Give the crystals emissive cores and a lighter rim so they read as a glowing resource
Add a metallic specular lobe to tank hull edges and tracks
Vary roof tile tint per tile row to break the uniform red

detail.reason: panel-1: Good density on the building: individual roof shingles with missing tiles, stone coursing, window frames with mullions, timber posts, a plinth course, sandbags, crates and barrels. The tank has tracks, road wheels and hatches. Weak spots: soldiers are blank-faced pegs, banners are flat planes, the portico interior is a dark void, and the sun emblem is a featureless disc. | panel-2: For an RTS set the density is good: individual roof tiles with missing ones, stone coursing, half-timber framing, window surrounds, banner fringe, tank hatches and tracks, sandbags, crates, barrels, a rutted road and tyre track decals. In the close-up the infantry carry packs and rifles but have no faces or hands, the hall has no door hardware, gutters or chimney, the wall panels repeat exactly, and the ground away from the road is a blank slab. | panel-3: Good density for an RTS base at LOD0: individual roof tiles, stone coursing, window mullions and sills, tank road wheels and hatches, soldiers with packs and rifles, sandbag stacks, crates, a fuel drum cluster and a cobbled road. Up close the soldiers are crude, the banner hangs without folds, and the wall coping is plain; the hall rear is bare.
fixes: Add faces, webbing and rifle detail to infantry
Give banners a faction emblem and cloth folds
Model a door with planks and hardware inside the portico; emboss the gable emblem
Add helmet rims, faces and hands to the infantry at LOD0
Add door ironwork, a lantern and a gutter line to the hall
Break the wall with a damaged or capped section and vary the panel joints
Scatter ground detail: paving joints, grass tufts at the wall base, puddles, a few stones
Add cloth folds to the banners and a fringe/emblem
Add downpipes, chimney and a rear door/loading bay to the hall
Give soldiers helmets with a brim and readable weapon shapes

wear.reason: panel-1: Some story: missing roof tiles, rust staining on the tank, dirt at the building base, dark streaks on stone. But the concrete barriers and ground are pristine, no tyre tracks lead to the tank, the crystal node has no mining debris or scorching, and the stone is evenly clean. | panel-2: There is deliberate story: missing and slipped roof tiles, streak stains under the windows, mud on the tank's lower hull, chipped red paint on the turret, ruts and a curved track mark on the ground, sandbags and supply crates. It stays even and mild: the walls are clean near the base, banners are pristine apart from the fringe, the perimeter wall has no damage, and nothing records which way the weather or the traffic comes from. | panel-3: Missing and slipped roof tiles, rusted tank hull lower edges, streaking under windows, darkened wall bases, tire tracks across the yard and a cracked rock under the crystals tell a used, garrisoned base. Paved yard and perimeter wall are a little too clean.
fixes: Add tyre/track ruts from the tank bay across the yard
Stain and chip the barriers; add moss and water streaks under the tower windows
Scatter mined crystal shards and dust around the resource node
Add splash dirt and moss at the base of the hall and towers
Fade and tear one banner
Chip a corner of the perimeter wall and stain it below the coping
Darken the ground in front of the door and around the tank bay with oil and foot traffic
Add soot above a chimney or the lit windows
Add oil stains and track ruts where the tank is parked
Chip the wall coping corners and add moss/dirt at the wall base

lod.reason: panel-1: LOD2 at 3.9k keeps the outline, roof colour, towers, banners, tank, squad and crystals; the switch would be near-invisible at RTS camera distance. Losses: windows become flat yellow rectangles without frames, tower stone coursing and timber framing vanish, roof becomes a flat red plane, and the gable sun disc disappears. | panel-2: LOD2 at 3.9k keeps the full outline and every colour block: red roofs, stone hall, banners, tank with red turret top, squad, crystals, road and walls. Losses that would show: the gold emblem disc on the gable and the tower finials vanish, the half-timber framing and gable trim on the front disappear leaving a flat wall, the windows change from mullioned frames to bare orange rectangles of a different shape, the crystal cluster drops from many shards to a few and the rock shrinks, and the wall loses its coping shape. | panel-3: LOD2 at 3.9k keeps every major silhouette and colour block: towers, roof, porch, banners, windows (now flat yellow squares), tank, troops, crystals and walls. The roof gable glyph and tower finials drop and the stone texture flattens, but at RTS distance the switch is near invisible.
fixes: Bake stone coursing and timber framing into LOD2 vertex colour/texture
Keep the gable emblem as a flat decal at LOD2
Keep the gable emblem as one coloured quad or vertex-colour disc at LOD2
Keep the finials as a single thin prism each
Paint the timber frame and gable trim into LOD2 vertex colour
Match LOD2 window size and position to the LOD0 openings
Keep the largest five crystals and the full rock footprint
Keep the tower finials as single spikes at LOD2 since they break the skyline
Bake mullion lines into the LOD2 window quads so the windows do not turn into plain yellow squares

technical.reason: panel-1: QA clean and the LOD2 budget is excellent for an RTS building. But 130k triangles at LOD0 is very heavy for a piece seen from a strategy camera; much is spent on individual shingles and stone blocks that read as texture at play distance, while infantry remain crude. | panel-2: QA is clean and the LOD2 budget is right for an RTS set. But 130k triangles at LOD0 is heavy for a scene seen from an RTS camera: the detail map shows density saturated across the whole hall and walls, much of it in individually modelled roof tiles and stone courses that could be texture, while the infantry that players look at are crude. The 34:1 drop from LOD0 to LOD2 leaves a large jump for LOD1 to cover. | panel-3: QA clean. LOD2 is excellent value. LOD0 at 130k triangles is heavy for a single RTS building that will be seen from a high camera; many triangles go into individual roof tiles and wall stones that are mostly sub-pixel at gameplay zoom, and LOD1 at 33k is still large.
fixes: Replace modelled shingles and stone blocks with a normal-mapped trim at LOD0; target ~40k
Spend the saved budget on infantry silhouettes and the tank turret
Move roof tiles and stone coursing to the trim sheet normal at LOD0, keeping modelled tiles only at eaves and for the broken ones
Target roughly 60-80k for LOD0 and spend some of the saving on the infantry
Instance wall segments and soldiers so they share geometry
Check that the draw count for moving parts (turret, banners) is within budget
Replace modelled roof tiles with a tiled texture/normal on LOD0 except along the eaves and ridge, cutting ~40k triangles
Target LOD1 near 12-15k by gating wall stone geometry
